from.place: Lemma 05SU(2): LF is compatible with shifts

title: Left derived values commute with shifts
statement: In Situation 05S8 [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal D$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$. Then $LF$ is defined at $X$ if and only if it is defined at $X[n]$, and in this case there is a canonical isomorphism $LF(X)[n]\to LF(X[n])$ between values.

proof.text: For every integer n, sending a denominator s:X'\to X in S/X to its shifted morphism s[n]:X'[n]\to X[n] defines an equivalence S/X\simeq S/X[n]. The forward implication that s[n] lies in S is the shift-compatibility axiom (MS5) in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], and the reverse implication follows by applying the same axiom to -n; identities and commuting triangles are preserved by the shift automorphism.

source.place: Lemma 05SU(2), proof from the shift automorphism and MS5

proof.text: Write G:S/X\to\mathcal D' for s:X'\mapsto F(X') and G_n:S/X[n]\to\mathcal D' for t:X''\mapsto F(X''). Exactness of F supplies the canonical shift isomorphisms F(X')[n]\cong F(X'[n]); hence, after the equivalence in Step 1, G_n is naturally isomorphic to the postcomposition of G by the shift [n] on \mathcal D'. Postcomposition by this automorphism preserves the cone, retraction, and factorization conditions in the definition of an essentially constant pro-object. Therefore G is essentially constant with value LF(X) if and only if G_n is essentially constant with value LF(X)[n].

source.place: Lemma 05SU(2), proof of the LF clause

proof.text: The equivalence of denominator categories and the transported cone identify the value at X[n] with LF(X)[n]. This gives the canonical isomorphism LF(X)[n]\to LF(X[n]); applying the construction with -n gives the converse implication, so LF is defined at X exactly when it is defined at X[n].
